profile.summary: I'm a consumer-facing growth PM who has owned the full funnel — from new user activation and conversion, through rewards and referrals, to post-purchase experience and operational infrastructure. At NewMe I wore three distinct product hats: growth, customer experience, and omnichannel platform. Before that, I worked on lifecycle and dealer products at Spinny and B2B CRM tooling at Anarock. My background is in data and analytics, which shapes how I discover problems, design experiments, and measure success. I build AI-powered workflows into my own process and think natively about how AI can be embedded into products.

growth.ownership: New user conversion across web and mobile, rewards program, referral program, A/B experimentation on checkout and offers

key_projects.name: Day 0 Offer Strategy
key_projects.problem: New users were not converting on their first session. Baseline Day 0 conversion was low and flat across cohorts.
key_projects.solution: Designed cohort-based, session-wise and time-bound escalating discounts — 15% → 20% → 25% — with urgency windows to drive first purchase. A/B tested against a flat discount control.
key_projects.impact: ~10% lift in Day 0 conversion, ~5% uplift in overall new-user conversion rate. Contribution margin protected via minimum order value floors.
key_projects.how_measured: A/B test comparing escalating cohort vs flat offer. Tracked Day 0 CVR, overall new-user CVR, and CM2 per cohort.

key_projects.name: Rewards Program (Trend Coins)
key_projects.problem: M3 retention was weak — users were not forming repeat purchase habits.
key_projects.solution: Designed and launched Trend Coins, a unified reward currency. Coin value set at ₹0.10. Included both transactional earning (orders) and non-transactional earning (profile completion, reviews). Ran a randomised A/B test to isolate the rewards program's independent effect.
key_projects.impact: 8% M3 retention lift attributable to the rewards program in isolation (via A/B test). The overall retention metric improved ~22% during the period, but that blended in seasonal and campaign effects — the isolated lift from rewards alone is 8%.
key_projects.important_distinction: Always cite 8% as the validated causal lift from rewards. The 22% is a blended metric across the period and overstates the program's independent contribution.
key_projects.how_measured: Randomised A/B test with rewards vs no-rewards cohorts. Tracked M3 retention as primary metric, with rewards tab views and enrollment rate as leading indicators.

key_projects.name: Referral Program
key_projects.problem: High CAC and limited organic acquisition channel.
key_projects.solution: Built a two-sided referral loop rewarding both referrer and referee. Tied rewards to first order completion, not just signup.
key_projects.impact: +12% signups, +3% daily orders, positive CM2 impact.
key_projects.how_measured: Tracked referral-attributed signups, first-order conversion from referrals, incremental daily order volume, and CM2 impact post-referral reward cost.

key_projects.name: Checkout A/B Experiments
key_projects.problem: Drop-off between cart and order placement.
key_projects.solution: Ran structured A/B experiments on checkout flow — copy, friction reduction, prepaid incentives.
key_projects.how_measured: A/B test on checkout variants, primary metric checkout-to-order rate.

post_purchase_cx.ownership: Returns, exchanges, delivery tracking, customer support, payment gateway integrations

key_projects.name: Support Automation (Bot + Ticketing)
key_projects.problem: Query resolution rate was 20%. Support was manual, slow, and creating high CSAT drag. Return requests were handled by agents without any risk profiling.
key_projects.solution: Implemented Kapture bot and ticketing system. Built a risk-profile model that automatically approved returns for 60–65% of users classified as low-risk, backtested at 95% agent approval rate. This freed agents to handle complex cases.
key_projects.how_measured: Resolution rate = queries auto-resolved / total queries raised. CSAT tracked post-interaction. Return CSAT tracked separately.
key_projects.stakeholder_conflict: Support ops wanted maximum automation; risk ops flagged abuse risk on blanket return approvals. Resolved by introducing the risk-profiling layer — automated for low-risk users, human-in-loop for flagged profiles.

key_projects.name: Payment Gateway Integrations
key_projects.problem: Fragmented refund flows across gateways causing customer confusion and repeat support queries.
key_projects.solution: Drove 3rd-party payment integrations across 3 gateways, standardising refund flows and communication.

omnichannel_platform.ownership: POS system, inventory management, auto-replenishment system for retail stores

key_projects.name: POS & Inventory Management System (0→1)
key_projects.problem: Retail stores were running on expensive third-party tools with no integration to central inventory. ₹50L+ in annual recurring licensing and operational costs. Store managers lacked visibility into stock, leading to stockouts and overstock.
key_projects.solution: Did store visits pre-discovery to understand workflows firsthand. Defined requirements, user flows, and rollout strategy in close collaboration with biz, design, and engineering. Built an end-to-end in-house POS and inventory management system from zero.
key_projects.impact: ₹50L+ annual recurring costs eliminated. Planning efficiency improved 30%+. Store margins improved ~3%.
key_projects.how_measured: Cost savings tracked against prior licensing invoices. Planning efficiency measured via stock accuracy and replenishment cycle time. Margin improvement tracked per store cohort post-rollout.
key_projects.differentiator: Started with store visits before writing a single requirement — this is what made the product fit actual workflows rather than imagined ones.

key_projects.name: Auto Replenishment System (ARS) Optimisation
key_projects.problem: Replenishment logic was not accounting for real-time sell-through rates, leading to planning inefficiencies.
key_projects.solution: Optimised ARS rules and triggers based on sell-through data.

faq.why_leave_newme: NewMe scaled into offline retail, which made the product surface more operational. I want to go deeper on consumer growth and AI-native product problems — that's where my energy is and where I think I have the most to contribute.
faq.biggest_achievement: Building the POS system from zero — not because it was technically hard, but because I started with store visits, not specs. That discovery-first approach is what made it actually work in practice.
faq.how_you_work_with_eng: I come to engineering with a clear problem statement and user context, not a feature list. I involve engineers early in discovery so they can shape the solution, not just execute it. At NewMe, the POS system architecture was co-designed with the eng lead based on what we both saw in stores.
faq.how_you_use_data: I define a metric pair before building — a leading indicator I can observe in days and a lagging outcome I care about. For rewards, that was rewards tab views + enrollment rate (leading) and M3 retention (lagging). The leading indicator tells me if the product is being used; the lagging indicator tells me if it's working.
faq.ai_in_your_work: I use n8n to automate lead-sourcing workflows, Claude for structured thinking and writing, and Lovable for fast UI prototyping. I also built a Claude-powered skill for job tracking. But more importantly, I think about how to embed AI natively into products — not as a chatbot bolt-on, but as the default interaction layer.
